fix(cli): enable WebSocket auth in AsyncAPI by populating IR auth schemes

## Description

Refs: Smallest AI WebSocket auth issue in API explorer

When AsyncAPI specs define security schemes, WebSocket channels should have `auth: true` in the IR **and** the IR's `auth.schemes` should be populated so auth scheme details flow through to FDR registration. Previously, WebSocket channels always had `auth: false` hardcoded across **three separate code paths**, and the AsyncAPI converter never called `addAuthToIR()`, which meant:
1. Authenticated WebSocket endpoints never displayed auth inputs in the docs playground
2. Even with `auth: true`, the `authSchemes` map registered to FDR was empty, so the fern-platform v1→v2 migration had nothing to resolve against

## Changes Made

### `AsyncAPIConverter` — populate IR auth schemes (NEW)
- Added `convertSecuritySchemes()` to the `convert()` pipeline (after `convertServers()`, before `convertChannels()`)
- If `authOverrides` exists (from `generators.yml` `auth-schemes`), converts via `convertApiAuth()` and calls `addAuthToIR()`
- Otherwise, iterates `components.securitySchemes` from the AsyncAPI spec and converts each natively
- New `convertSecurityScheme()` handles bearer, basic, apiKey (header), and oauth2 scheme types, following the same pattern as the OpenAPI `SecuritySchemeConverter`

### `asyncapi-to-ir` type updates
- Added `securitySchemes?: Record ` to `components` in both `DocumentV2` and `DocumentV3`
- Added `security` field to `ServerV3` and `ServerV2` type interfaces

### `asyncapi-to-ir` channel converters — set `auth: true`
- Added `hasServerSecurity()` private method to both `ChannelConverter3_0` and `ChannelConverter2_X` that checks if any server referenced by the channel defines security schemes
- Changed `auth: false` → `auth: this.hasServerSecurity() || this.context.authOverrides?.auth != null` in both converters

- In `buildChannel.ts`, replaced hardcoded `auth: false` with `auth: context.authOverrides?.auth != null || (context.ir.security != null && context.ir.security.length > 0)` — sets auth when either explicitly configured via `generators.yml` or the spec's own IR has security schemes populated

-------

    Generates TypeDoc documentation for a specific version tag and commits it to the gh-pages branch. The script uses git worktrees to isolate the documentation generation process from the main workspace.

    Documentation for each release is stored in a versioned directory (e.g., `v1.2.3/`) on the gh-pages branch. The script:

    - Parses semantic versions from tag names, ignoring arbitrary prefixes (e.g., tags `1.2.3`, `v1.2.3`, and `release-1.2.3` all create `v1.2.3/`)
    - Creates the gh-pages branch as an orphan branch if it doesn't exist

perf(ci): Reduce CI test time for faster PR feedback

## Problem

CI tests currently take 40+ minutes wall-clock time on PRs, which slows development iteration. The main bottlenecks are:

1. **Coverage collection** adds ~15-20 min overhead (11+ min just for `Combine coverage` step)
2. **16 PHP/DB matrix configurations** run on every PR
3. **60-second sleep** waiting for MySQL instead of health check
4. **Redundant PHP version testing** across multiple workflows
5. **No path filtering** on major workflows - PHP tests run even for doc-only changes

## Proposed Changes

### High Impact

- **Move coverage to scheduled/merge jobs** - Coverage isn't needed on every PR. Run it nightly or on merge to master.
- **Reduce PR test matrix** - Test 2-3 representative configs on PRs (e.g., PHP 8.4+MariaDB 11.8, PHP 8.2+MariaDB 11.8, PHP 8.4+MySQL 8.4). Run full 16-config matrix on master/releases only.
- **Replace `sleep 60` with health check** - Use `mysqladmin ping` in a loop instead of unconditional 60-second wait.
- **Add path-based filtering to major workflows** - Skip irrelevant CI runs entirely (see table below).

### Medium Impact

- **Use `skip-slow-tests` label inversely** - Skip E2E/full matrix by default; add labels like `needs-e2e` or `needs-full-matrix` when required.
- **Reduce PHP version matrix for syntax/isolated tests** - Test oldest + newest supported versions instead of all 5.
- **Pre-built Docker images** - Maintain images with OpenEMR pre-installed to skip initialization time.

### Quick Wins

- **Parallelize PHP syntax checking** - Use `xargs -P` for parallel linting.
- **Share vendor cache across workflows** - Multiple workflows run identical `composer install`.

## Path Filtering Suggestions

Several workflows already use `paths:` filtering (hadolint, shellcheck, codecov, composer-require-checker), but the major time-consuming workflows don't.

| Workflow | Trigger only on |
|----------|-----------------|
| Test / Test All | `**.php`, `**.inc`, `composer.*`, `package*.json`, `ci/**`, `docker/**`, `tests/**` |
| PHPStan | `**.php`, `**.inc`, `phpstan.*`, `.phpstan/**` |
| Rector | `**.php`, `**.inc`, `rector.php` |
| Styling (PHP) | `**.php`, `**.inc`, `.php-cs-fixer.*` |
| Styling (JS) | `**.js`, `**.mjs`, `.eslint*` |
| Styling (CSS) | `**.css`, `**.scss`, `.stylelint*` |
| Syntax | `**.php`, `**.inc` |
| JS Unit Test | `**.js`, `**.mjs`, `**.ts`, `package*.json` |
| SQL Lint | `**.sql`, `.sqruff*` |
| Semgrep | `**.php`, `**.js`, `**.py`, `.semgrep*` |

For more granular control within a workflow (e.g., skip E2E if only unit test files changed), [tj-actions/changed-files](https://github.com/tj-actions/changed-files) can conditionally skip jobs.

## Expected Outcome

Reduce typical PR CI time from 40+ minutes to ~15 minutes while maintaining test coverage quality on merge/release branches.

Simplify Daytona snapshot naming to use commit hash

Replace complex stage-based snapshot naming with simple commit hash naming for deterministic lookups.

## Changes
- Daytona snapshots now named `iterate-sandbox-{commitHash}` 
- Removed prefix-based resolution and expensive API listing
- Made `DAYTONA_SNAPSHOT_NAME` required (set to commit SHA in CI)
- Requires clean checkout to build snapshots

## Impact
Production deploys are now simpler: CI builds the snapshot with the commit hash and passes that directly to the worker, eliminating the need for snapshot resolution logic.

 

> [!NOTE]
> Streamlines Daytona snapshot handling to deterministic, commit-SHA–based names and wires this through CI, deploy, and tests.
> 
> - Adds reusable `./.github/workflows/build-snapshot.yml` to build once and output `snapshot_name`; used by `ci`, `deploy`, and `spec` jobs

> - Removes `backend/integrations/daytona/snapshot-resolver.ts` and all prefix-based resolution usages

> - Changes snapshot build script to enforce `SANDBOX_ITERATE_REPO_REF` as a 40-char commit SHA, name snapshots `iterate-sandbox-{commitSha}`, and handle already-exists idempotently
> - Updates tests (`daytona*.test.ts`) and specs workflow to consume the built snapshot name directly
